questions.q: George Winter's 1962 landmark experiment on wound healing demonstrated that superficial wounds kept moist healed faster than air-dried wounds. Which of the following mechanisms best explains this accelerated healing?
opts: Increased bacterial colonization promoting inflammatory response
Enhanced keratinocyte migration across the moist wound surface
Reduced growth factor concentration at the wound site
questions.exp: A moist environment promotes healing primarily by facilitating keratinocyte migration, as epidermal cells can easily glide across a moist surface but cannot traverse a dry scab or eschar. This principle, demonstrated by Winter in 1962, showed wounds healed twice as fast when kept moist.

questions.q: A 35-year-old man has a 4 cm linear scar crossing the cheek perpendicular to the relaxed skin tension lines without any contracture. Which scar revision technique is most appropriate?
opts: Z-plasty to lengthen and reorient the scar
Punch excision of the entire scar
questions.exp: W-plasty is indicated for long linear scars that cross RSTLs perpendicularly and require camouflage rather than lengthening. It converts the scar into a regularly irregular zigzag pattern without providing tissue lengthening, making it ideal when contracture release is not needed.

questions.q: A 45-year-old farmer presents with a verrucous plaque on the dorsum of his hand that developed 3 weeks after handling cattle. He has a history of treated pulmonary tuberculosis 10 years ago. Biopsy shows caseating granulomas with acid-fast bacilli. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Tuberculosis verrucosa cutis occurs following exogenous inoculation of M. tuberculosis in a previously sensitized (immune) individual. The verrucous morphology at the site of direct contact in a patient with prior TB infection is characteristic of this form of cutaneous TB.

questions.q: A patient with extensive lower limb venous disease has incompetent great saphenous vein reflux along with visible reticular veins and telangiectasias. According to the principles of sclerotherapy, which vessels should be treated first?
opts: Telangiectasias as they are most cosmetically bothersome
Reticular veins as they are the feeding vessels for telangiectasias
Great saphenous vein at the point of highest reflux
All vessels simultaneously using foam sclerotherapy
questions.exp: A fundamental rule of sclerotherapy is to always treat the highest point of reflux first, such as incompetent saphenous junctions, before treating distal smaller tributaries like reticular veins and telangiectasias.

questions.q: A 58-year-old man presents with a 0.8 cm well-defined nodular lesion on his upper back, biopsy-proven as nodular basal cell carcinoma. He is immunocompetent with no prior skin cancers. If curettage and electrodesiccation is chosen as treatment, how many complete scrape-and-burn cycles should be performed?
questions.exp: For malignant lesions treated with curettage and electrodesiccation, the scrape-and-burn sequence must be strictly repeated for 3 standard cycles to ensure adequate tumor destruction. This is different from benign lesions which typically require only a single cycle.

questions.q: A 6-month-old male infant presents with fine, white scales on extensor surfaces of limbs and trunk with sparing of flexures. Examination reveals hyperlinear palms and keratosis pilaris. Skin biopsy shows orthokeratotic hyperkeratosis with absent granular layer. Which gene is most likely mutated?
questions.exp: The clinical features of fine white scales with flexural sparing, hyperlinear palms, keratosis pilaris, and histopathology showing absent granular layer are pathognomonic of Ichthyosis Vulgaris. This condition is caused by loss-of-function mutations in the FLG (filaggrin) gene with semi-dominant inheritance.
questions.source: Ichthyoses – Classification, Clinical Features and Management

questions.q: A 45-year-old woman undergoes botulinum toxin injection for glabellar lines. Two weeks later, she presents with right upper eyelid ptosis. Which injection error most likely caused this complication?
opts: Injection placed too superficially in the procerus muscle
Injection placed below the bony orbital rim at the midpupillary line
Excessive dose used in the lateral corrugator belly
Injection directed tangentially rather than perpendicularly
questions.exp: Upper eyelid ptosis is the most feared complication of glabellar injections, caused by toxin diffusion through the orbital septum into the levator palpebrae superioris muscle. This occurs when injections are placed below the bony orbital rim or at the midpupillary line, violating the critical safety principle of staying strictly above the orbital rim.

questions.q: A 62-year-old man is diagnosed with basal cell carcinoma. Molecular analysis reveals constitutive activation of the Hedgehog signaling pathway. Which of the following genetic alterations is MOST commonly responsible for this pathway activation in sporadic BCC?
opts: Loss-of-function mutation in PTCH1 tumor suppressor gene
questions.exp: Loss-of-function mutations or deletions of the PTCH1 tumor suppressor gene on chromosome 9q22 are found in 70-90% of sporadic BCCs, making it the most common genetic alteration. PTCH1 normally inhibits SMO, and its loss leads to unchecked SMO activity and constitutive Hedgehog pathway activation.

questions.q: Which component of the mycobacterial cell wall is primarily responsible for inhibiting phagolysosome fusion within host macrophages, thereby ensuring intracellular survival?
questions.exp: Lipoarabinomannan (LAM) is a major structural lipoglycan that critically inhibits phagolysosome fusion and scavenges reactive oxygen species, directly ensuring intracellular survival of mycobacteria within macrophages. Cord factor primarily induces mitochondrial toxicity and granuloma formation.

questions.q: A 35-year-old man with chronic plaque psoriasis is being evaluated for biologic therapy. Which cytokine axis is primarily responsible for the recruitment of neutrophils that form Munro microabscesses in psoriatic lesions?
opts: IL-17/IL-22 axis inducing chemokines and antimicrobial peptides
IL-10 axis promoting regulatory T cell function
questions.exp: IL-17 and IL-22, produced by Th17 cells and other immune cells, induce chemokines and antimicrobial peptides that attract neutrophils to the epidermis, forming the characteristic Munro microabscesses seen in psoriasis.

questions.q: A 45-year-old diabetic patient presents with a chronic venous leg ulcer that has failed to heal despite 8 weeks of standard care. On examination, the wound bed shows yellow adherent slough with minimal granulation tissue. According to the TIME framework of wound bed preparation, which component should be addressed first in this patient?
questions.exp: The TIME framework prioritizes Tissue management (T) as the first step, involving debridement of non-viable tissue, slough, or necrotic eschar that acts as a physical barrier to healing and harbors bacteria. In this case, the yellow adherent slough must be addressed before other interventions can be effective.

questions.q: A 45-year-old solid organ transplant recipient presents with multiple skin lesions. Compared to an immunocompetent individual, which of the following statements regarding the relative frequency of keratinocyte carcinomas in this patient is TRUE?
opts: BCC remains more common than SCC as in immunocompetent patients
SCC becomes more common than BCC, reversing the usual ratio
Melanoma becomes the most common skin malignancy
The BCC to SCC ratio remains unchanged but absolute numbers increase equally
questions.exp: In immunocompetent individuals, BCC is more common than SCC. However, in solid organ transplant recipients, this ratio is reversed, with SCC becoming the most common post-transplant cutaneous malignancy despite an overall increased risk for both tumor types.

questions.q: In the early induction phase of lichen planus pathogenesis, plasmacytoid dendritic cells are activated via Toll-like receptors and release a key cytokine that initiates the inflammatory cascade. Which cytokine is released by these cells?
questions.exp: Plasmacytoid dendritic cells (pDCs) are stimulated via Toll-like receptors in the early phase of lichen planus and release Type 1 interferons, specifically IFN-α. This represents an early event in the cascade leading to T-cell mediated keratinocyte damage.

questions.q: A 3-year-old child presents with history of 8 episodes of pneumonia in the past year, two episodes of bacterial meningitis, and recurrent otitis media requiring IV antibiotics. Which mnemonic best describes the warning signs that should prompt evaluation for primary immunodeficiency?
questions.exp: SPUR stands for Serious, Persistent, Unusual, and Recurrent infections - the cardinal warning signs of primary immunodeficiency. This child demonstrates multiple features warranting immunological workup.

questions.q: A 35-year-old woman undergoes sclerotherapy for lower limb telangiectasias. The dermatologist uses a detergent sclerosant. Which mechanism best describes how this class of agents causes endothelial injury?
opts: Drawing water out of cells via osmotic gradient causing cellular dehydration
Disruption of the endothelial lipid bilayer through protein theft denaturation
Direct poisoning of cell surface proteins and disruption of chemical bonds
Mechanical shearing of endothelial cells through high-pressure injection
questions.exp: Detergent sclerosants are amphiphilic molecules that form micelles and disrupt the endothelial cell membrane by extracting cell surface proteins, a process termed 'protein theft denaturation.' This leads to rapid cell lysis and thrombosis.

questions.q: Which of the following clinical scenarios is LEAST consistent with the warning signs of primary immunodeficiency?
opts: A single episode of viral upper respiratory tract infection resolving in 5 days
Pneumonia caused by Pneumocystis jirovecii in a 6-month-old infant
Recurrent skin abscesses requiring surgical drainage since infancy
Persistent oral candidiasis unresponsive to standard antifungal therapy
questions.exp: A single self-limiting viral URTI is a normal childhood illness. Primary immunodeficiency is suspected when infections are Serious, Persistent, Unusual (opportunistic organisms), or Recurrent - none of which apply to a routine viral infection.

questions.q: A dermatologist plans to perform a biopsy on a pigmented lesion clinically suspicious for melanoma. Which biopsy modality is contraindicated in this scenario?
opts: Punch biopsy encompassing the entire lesion
Incisional biopsy of the thickest portion if excision is impractical
questions.exp: Shave biopsy is contraindicated in suspected melanoma because it compromises accurate assessment of Breslow thickness, which is critical for staging and prognosis. Excisional biopsy is the gold standard for suspected melanoma as it allows complete margin and depth evaluation.

questions.q: An 18-year-old male presents with large, dirty-brown, polygonal adherent scales predominantly over the neck and trunk. His mother reports she had prolonged labour during his delivery. Slit-lamp examination reveals corneal opacities. What is the most likely inheritance pattern?
questions.exp: The 'dirty neck' sign with large polygonal brown scales, corneal opacities, and history of prolonged labour in the carrier mother are characteristic of X-linked Ichthyosis (XLI). This condition is X-linked recessive, caused by STS gene deletion, affecting males while females are carriers.
questions.source: Ichthyoses – Classification, Clinical Features and Management

questions.q: A 28-year-old woman presents with multiple ice-pick acne scars on her cheeks, each measuring approximately 1.5 mm in width. Which punch technique is most appropriate, and what is the recommended direction of traction during closure?
opts: Punch elevation with traction parallel to RSTLs
Punch excision with traction perpendicular to RSTLs
Punch replacement grafting with traction parallel to RSTLs
Punch elevation with no traction required
questions.exp: Punch excision is the best technique for narrow ice-pick scars <2 mm wide. Outward traction is applied perpendicular to the relaxed skin tension lines (RSTLs) to convert the circular defect into an ellipse, which is then closed with a single superficial suture.

questions.q: A dermatologic surgeon is planning electrosurgery on a patient with a cardiac pacemaker. Which of the following is the safest approach to minimize electromagnetic interference?
opts: Use monopolar electrosurgery keeping the electrode at least 5 cm from the pacemaker
Use monopolar electrosurgery with increased power settings for shorter duration
Position the grounding pad directly over the pacemaker site
questions.exp: Bipolar forceps are the preferred modality in patients with pacemakers because current passes only between the two tips of the forceps with no systemic current spread, eliminating the risk of electromagnetic interference. Monopolar electrosurgery should be avoided within 15 cm of a pacemaker.

questions.q: A 45-year-old woman presents with pruritic, violaceous, polygonal papules on her wrists and ankles. Histopathology reveals a band-like lymphocytic infiltrate at the dermo-epidermal junction with apoptotic keratinocytes. Which cells are primarily responsible for inducing basal keratinocyte apoptosis in this condition?
opts: CD4+ T-helper cells in the dermis
CD8+ cytotoxic T-cells in proximity to basal keratinocytes
CD1a+ Langerhans cells in the epidermis
questions.exp: In lichen planus, CD8+ cytotoxic T-cells are located in close proximity to damaged basal keratinocytes and are the primary effectors responsible for inducing keratinocyte apoptosis. CD4+ T-helper cells are predominantly found in the dermis and provide supportive signals.

questions.q: A patient presents with a painless, lobulated, strawberry-like mass in the nasal cavity that bleeds profusely on touch. The characteristic white pinpoint dots visible on the surface of the lesion represent which of the following?
opts: Keratin pearls within the hyperplastic epithelium
questions.exp: The pathognomonic 'strawberry-like' appearance of rhinosporidiosis lesions is due to white pinpoint dots on the surface, which represent mature sporangia packed with endospores visible through the hyperplastic epithelium. This highly vascular polyp bleeds easily upon manipulation.

questions.q: A 12-year-old boy from a rural endemic area presents with a single hypopigmented, hypoesthetic patch on his forearm. His father was treated for multibacillary leprosy 3 years ago. What is the approximate increased risk of this child acquiring leprosy compared to a child without any family contact?
questions.exp: A child's risk of acquiring leprosy is estimated to be 9 times higher if there is a family member contact. The risk increases to 14 times if the index case is specifically the mother or a multibacillary patient.

questions.q: A 45-year-old woman presents with a tense bulla on her forearm. You suspect bullous pemphigoid and plan to perform a biopsy for direct immunofluorescence (DIF). Which of the following is the most appropriate technique and specimen handling?
opts: Biopsy from the center of the bulla, placed in 10% formalin
Biopsy from perilesional skin, placed in Michel's medium
Shave biopsy from the roof of the bulla, placed in normal saline
Biopsy from an old, crusted bulla, placed in Zeus medium
questions.exp: For DIF in bullous diseases, a biopsy must be taken from perilesional skin (not the blister center or old lesions) to avoid secondary re-epithelialization changes. The specimen must be placed in Michel's medium, Zeus medium, or normal saline—never formalin, which destroys immunoglobulins.

questions.q: A patient treated with botulinum toxin for forehead horizontal lines develops an exaggerated lateral brow elevation giving a 'Spock-like' appearance. What is the underlying mechanism for this cosmetic complication?
opts: Over-treatment of the glabellar complex causing compensatory frontalis hyperactivity
Unopposed lateral frontalis fibers when central frontalis is treated alone
Migration of toxin into the corrugator supercilii muscle
Asymmetric treatment of the procerus muscle
questions.exp: The 'Spock' or 'quizzical' brow appearance occurs when the central frontalis muscle is adequately treated while the lateral fibers remain active and unopposed. This causes compensatory, unnatural lateral brow elevation. Leaving lateral fibers slightly active is intentional for brow support, but complete central paralysis creates this distinctive deformity.

questions.q: In epidemiological surveys, childhood leprosy (0-14 years) is considered an important indicator because:
opts: Children have stronger immunity making diagnosis easier
It reflects active ongoing transmission in the community
Childhood leprosy always presents as multibacillary type
Children are the primary reservoir of Mycobacterium leprae
questions.exp: Children typically have a restricted geographic range of movement, so the incidence of childhood leprosy serves as a robust marker of active, ongoing, and recent transmission of M. leprae within the community, indicating presence of undetected infectious cases nearby.

questions.q: A 28-year-old male rice farmer from Tamil Nadu presents with unilateral nasal obstruction, recurrent epistaxis, and mucoid discharge for 6 months. Examination reveals a friable, red, pedunculated mass with tiny white pinpoint dots on its surface. Which of the following statements regarding the causative organism is correct?
opts: It can be readily cultured on Sabouraud dextrose agar
It belongs to the Mesomycetozoa clade and is an aquatic protist
It is transmitted primarily through respiratory droplets
It is a dimorphic fungus with yeast and hyphal forms
questions.exp: Rhinosporidium seeberi, the causative agent of rhinosporidiosis, was previously misclassified as a fungus but is now recognized as an aquatic eukaryotic protist belonging to the Mesomycetozoa clade. It cannot be cultured in vitro on artificial media and is transmitted through contaminated stagnant water.

questions.q: Which histopathological feature best distinguishes subacute cutaneous lupus erythematosus (SCLE) from discoid lupus erythematosus (DLE)?
opts: Prominent follicular plugging and basement membrane thickening
Absence of hyperkeratosis and dermal fibrosis
questions.exp: SCLE characteristically shows little or no hyperkeratosis, basement membrane thickening, follicular plugging, or dermal fibrosis, which are features more prominent in DLE. Both conditions show interface dermatitis, but DLE additionally demonstrates follicular involvement and scarring.

questions.q: Which epithelial cell-derived cytokine is crucial for driving naive T helper cells toward the Th2 differentiation pathway in atopic dermatitis?
questions.exp: TSLP and IL-33 are key epithelial cell-secreted cytokines that drive Th0 cells towards the Th2 differentiation pathway, which is fundamental to the pathogenesis of atopic dermatitis.

questions.q: A 35-year-old woman presents with annular, scaly, erythematous plaques on her upper back and arms that worsen with sun exposure. She has no joint pain or nephritis. Biopsy shows interface dermatitis with vacuolar degeneration, epidermal atrophy, and dermal mucin deposition without follicular plugging or basement membrane thickening. Which autoantibody is most likely to be positive?
questions.exp: This presentation is classic for subacute cutaneous lupus erythematosus (SCLE), characterized by photosensitive annular or papulosquamous lesions with interface dermatitis and prominent mucin deposition. SCLE is frequently associated with anti-SSA/Ro autoantibodies.
